column1: # The recall corpus: real documentation bugs found by hand in repositories
# where kibble tested nothing, each pinned to the commit the bug was found at
# and to the line a reader trips on. repos.tsv proves kibble does not invent
# failures and mutations.tsv proves it catches rot planted on purpose. This
# file holds what neither can: rot that was already there and that kibble
# walked past, reading the repository as fine.
# A row is caught when the run reports the wanted status on that bug: an
# example line in the named document whose status is wanted and whose
# command or detail contains the proof, or a top-level row whose status is
# wanted and whose detail contains the proof. The JSON carries no line
# number, so the line column says where a person should look and the proof
# pins identity, as in mutations.tsv. Wanted statuses are separated by "|".
# caught=no rows are the scoreboard: the job prints whether each is caught now
# and never fails on them. Once a change catches a row, flip it to caught=yes,
# and from then on the job fails if the line stops reaching its status. Every
# bug found by hand becomes a row here before any fix for it is built.
# The first four came from the 2026-10-22 hand check of ten repositories
# kibble had run nothing on. Columns are tab-separated:
# name, clone URL, pinned commit, document, line, wanted status, proof, caught.
